speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent camping trip in Minnesota and the pattern of migrating joint pain, have you noticed a red, expanding "bullseye" rash on any part of your body, or felt bitten by a tick? REQUEST TEST: Lyme_Disease_Serology

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the Lyme serology is normal, I need to rule out other causes like gonococcal arthritis or viral exanthems. Do you have any pain or discharge in your urethra, and have you noticed any pus-filled or blistering lesions on your skin? REQUEST TEST: Joint_Aspirate_Gram_Stain

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of Gram-negative diplococci in the joint aspirate is highly suggestive of Disseminated Gonococcal Infection. Given your sexual history, this confirms the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection
